summary:
The Improving Federal Building Security Act of 2024 (Pub. L. 118-157, enacted December 17, 2024, originating as S. 3613), codified as a note to 40 U.S.C. 1315, establishes a mandatory response-and-reporting regime governing Facility Security Committees' (FSCs) treatment of security recommendations issued by the Federal Protective Service (FPS). The Act operates as freestanding law rather than by direct amendment to the U.S. Code.

Section 2(a) supplies definitions, incorporating the definition of "agency" from 5 U.S.C. 551, defining "Facility Security Committee" as a committee comprising representatives of all Federal tenants in a specific non-military facility, the facility's security organization, and the owning or leasing Federal tenant, responsible for addressing facility-specific security issues and approving security measures; and designating the Secretary of Homeland Security as "Secretary."

Section 2(b) imposes a 90-day deadline, running from FPS issuance of a security recommendation, within which the head of the FSC (or designee) must respond to the Secretary indicating adoption or rejection, describing the financial implications (including a benefit-cost characterization), and—if rejecting—providing justification for accepting the residual risk. Subsection (b)(2) directs the Secretary to develop a monitoring method and take reasonable action to ensure FSC responsiveness.

Section 2(c) requires an annual report, due not later than 270 days after enactment and annually thereafter, to the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and the House Committees on Homeland Security and on Transportation and Infrastructure. The report must, for the preceding fiscal year, summarize FPS recommendations; state acceptance and rejection percentages; state the percentage of FSCs failing to respond timely; summarize rejection justifications; summarize financial implications; analyze risk-mitigation steps taken upon rejection; and analyze trends. Reports are to be unclassified with an optional classified annex, accompanied by annual briefings to the same committees.

Section 2(d) requires the Secretary, not later than 180 days after enactment, to submit to the same committees an unredacted report on all surveillance technology recommended by FPS and any intended use.

Section 2(e) provides that no additional funds are authorized to be appropriated to carry out the Act (a negative authorization provision).

Section 2(f) sets a sunset: the Act ceases to be effective five years after enactment, and directs the Comptroller General to submit a report on the Act's effectiveness within the same five-year period.

Section 2(g) limits application to General Services Administration facilities under FPS protection and to non-GSA facilities that pay FPS protection fees.
